title: Climate Analog Search Tools
text: analogs R package provides flexible, computationally efficient tools analog-based climate change analyses. core function search “analog pool” data best match query site. Matching can based combination climatic similarity geographic distance, matches can processed variety ways. supports range analyses including analog-based climate change velocity, analog impact modeling, analog availability, analog intensity.

title: Analog intensity: weighted sum of analogs within climate/geographic limits — analog_intensity
text: x Focal locations analogs found. matrix/data.frame columns x, y, climate variables, SpatRaster climate variable layers. pool reference dataset search analogs. Either: Matrix/data.frame columns x, y, climate variables,     SpatRaster climate variable layers, analog_index object created     build_analog_index (repeated queries). max_clim Maximum climate distance constraint (default: NULL = climate constraint). Can either: scalar: Euclidean radius climate space (e.g., 0.5) vector: Per-variable absolute differences (length must equal     number climate variables) reference locations within climate distance considered. max_geog Maximum geographic distance constraint (default: NULL = geographic constraint). specified, reference locations within distance considered. Radius units specified kilometers coord_type = "lonlat", projected coordinate units coord_type = "projected". weight Weighting function matches, used mode "sum" "mean". One : "uniform": matches weighted equally (weight = 1.0). "inverse_clim": Weight = 1 / (climate_distance + epsilon),     epsilon given theta (small default theta     NULL). "inverse_geog": Weight = 1 / (geographic_distance + epsilon),     epsilon given theta (small default theta     NULL). "gaussian_clim": Gaussian kernel climate distance,     weight = exp(-climate_distance^2 / (2*sigma^2)), sigma (bandwidth)     given theta. "gaussian_geog": Gaussian kernel geographic distance,     weight = exp(-geographic_distance^2 / (2*sigma^2)), sigma (bandwidth)     given theta. "gaussian_joint": Bivariate Gaussian kernel (product     independent Gaussians climate geographic distances),     bandwidths given theta 2-element vector c(sigma_clim, sigma_geog). "inverse_joint": Joint inverse distance,     weight = 1 / sqrt((climate_distance + eps_clim)^2 + (geographic_distance + eps_geog)^2),     epsilon values given theta 2-element vector c(eps_clim, eps_geog). mode "knn_geog", "knn_clim", "count", "", weight must NULL. theta Optional numeric parameter used weighting functions mode "sum" "mean" weight "uniform". Interpretation depends weight: "inverse_clim" "inverse_geog": epsilon value     added distances (scalar; default: 1e-12 climate, 1e-6 geography). "gaussian_clim" "gaussian_geog": sigma bandwidth     parameter (scalar; larger values = slower decay distance). "gaussian_joint": 2-element vector c(sigma_clim, sigma_geog)     giving bandwidths climate geographic dimensions. "inverse_joint": 2-element vector c(eps_clim, eps_geog)     giving epsilon values climate geographic dimensions. theta NULL, sensible defaults used single-parameter weights. weight = "uniform" non-aggregating modes, theta must NULL. coord_type Coordinate system type (default: "auto"): "auto": Automatically detect coordinate ranges. "lonlat": Unprojected lon/lat coordinates (uses great-circle distance;     assumes max_geog km). "projected": Projected XY coordinates (uses planar distance;     assumes max_geog projection units). index_res Tuning parameter giving number bins per dimension internally-used lattice search index. Either: positive integer. "auto" (default): Automatically tune intex resolution     optimizing compute time subsample focal points. focal     relatively rows, auto-tuning skipped default resolution     16 used. Ignored pool analog_index (uses index's resolution). n_threads Optional integer number threads use computation. NULL (default), global RcppParallel setting used (see RcppParallel::setThreadOptions).

title: Find Climate Analogs — find_analogs
text: function uses spatial indexing structure (lattice-based) quickly search large reference datasets. Climate similarity measured using Euclidean distance climate space (ideally pre-whitened; see Details). Geographic distance can computed lon/lat coordinates (great-circle distance) projected coordinates (planar distance). **Common Use Cases:** Climate Velocity (nearest geographic neighbor similar climate): Climate Impact (climatically similar locations within dispersal range): Analog Availability (count suitable locations): Weighted Analog Intensity (e.g., distance-weighted availability): Using Pre-built Index (repeated queries):
code: find_analogs(   x        = clim$clim1,   pool     = clim$clim2,   mode     = "knn_geog",   max_clim = 0.5,   max_geog = NULL,   k        = 1 ) find_analogs(   x        = clim$clim1,   pool     = clim$clim2,   mode     = "knn_clim",   max_clim = 0.5,   max_geog = 100,   k        = 20 ) find_analogs(   x        = clim$clim1,   pool     = clim$clim1,   mode     = "count",   max_clim = 0.5,   max_geog = 100 ) find_analogs(   x        = clim$clim1,   pool     = clim$clim1,   mode     = "sum",   max_clim = 0.5,   max_geog = 100,   weight   = "inverse_geog",   theta    = 1e-6 ) # Build index once index <- build_analog_index(clim$clim2, index_res = 16)  # Query multiple times v1 <- find_analogs(x = sites1, pool = index, mode = "knn_geog", max_clim = 0.5, k = 1) v2 <- find_analogs(x = sites2, pool = index, mode = "knn_geog", max_clim = 0.3, k = 1)

title: Tune Index Resolution — tune_index_res
text: x Focal locations analogs found. matrix/data.frame columns x, y, climate variables, SpatRaster climate variable layers. pool reference dataset search analogs. Either: Matrix/data.frame columns x, y, climate variables,     SpatRaster climate variable layers, analog_index object created     build_analog_index (repeated queries). mode Character string specifying analog search mode. One : "knn_clim": focal, return k analogs     smallest climate distance, subject max_clim     max_geog filters. "knn_geog": focal, return k analogs     smallest geographic distance, subject max_clim     max_geog filters. "": Return analogs satisfy filters. "count": focal, count many analogs satisfy     filters. "sum": focal, sum weights analogs     satisfy filters (see weight theta). "mean": focal, mean weights analogs     satisfy filters. max_clim Maximum climate distance constraint (default: NULL = climate constraint). Can either: scalar: Euclidean radius climate space (e.g., 0.5) vector: Per-variable absolute differences (length must equal     number climate variables) reference locations within climate distance considered. max_geog Maximum geographic distance constraint (default: NULL = geographic constraint). specified, reference locations within distance considered. Radius units specified kilometers coord_type = "lonlat", projected coordinate units coord_type = "projected". k Number nearest analogs return per focal location kNN modes. Required mode "knn_geog" "knn_clim"; must NULL modes. weight Weighting function matches, used mode "sum" "mean". One : "uniform": matches weighted equally (weight = 1.0). "inverse_clim": Weight = 1 / (climate_distance + epsilon),     epsilon given theta (small default theta     NULL). "inverse_geog": Weight = 1 / (geographic_distance + epsilon),     epsilon given theta (small default theta     NULL). "gaussian_clim": Gaussian kernel climate distance,     weight = exp(-climate_distance^2 / (2*sigma^2)), sigma (bandwidth)     given theta. "gaussian_geog": Gaussian kernel geographic distance,     weight = exp(-geographic_distance^2 / (2*sigma^2)), sigma (bandwidth)     given theta. "gaussian_joint": Bivariate Gaussian kernel (product     independent Gaussians climate geographic distances),     bandwidths given theta 2-element vector c(sigma_clim, sigma_geog). "inverse_joint": Joint inverse distance,     weight = 1 / sqrt((climate_distance + eps_clim)^2 + (geographic_distance + eps_geog)^2),     epsilon values given theta 2-element vector c(eps_clim, eps_geog). mode "knn_geog", "knn_clim", "count", "", weight must NULL. theta Optional numeric parameter used weighting functions mode "sum" "mean" weight "uniform". Interpretation depends weight: "inverse_clim" "inverse_geog": epsilon value     added distances (scalar; default: 1e-12 climate, 1e-6 geography). "gaussian_clim" "gaussian_geog": sigma bandwidth     parameter (scalar; larger values = slower decay distance). "gaussian_joint": 2-element vector c(sigma_clim, sigma_geog)     giving bandwidths climate geographic dimensions. "inverse_joint": 2-element vector c(eps_clim, eps_geog)     giving epsilon values climate geographic dimensions. theta NULL, sensible defaults used single-parameter weights. weight = "uniform" non-aggregating modes, theta must NULL. coord_type Coordinate system type (default: "auto"): "auto": Automatically detect coordinate ranges. "lonlat": Unprojected lon/lat coordinates (uses great-circle distance;     assumes max_geog km). "projected": Projected XY coordinates (uses planar distance;     assumes max_geog projection units). n_threads Optional integer number threads use computation. NULL (default), global RcppParallel setting used (see RcppParallel::setThreadOptions). default_res Default resolution use starting point search. Default 16. verbose Logical; TRUE, print selected resolution. Default FALSE.

title: Tune Index Resolution — tune_index_res

title: Tune Index Resolution — tune_index_res
text: function uses adaptive bracketing algorithm: Starts three resolutions: default/2, default, default*2 Evaluates elapsed time minimum edge, expands search direction Returns resolution lowest elapsed time typically requires 3-5 query evaluations total, making much faster exhaustive grid search. function performs tuning non-trivial problem sizes (>2000 focal points). smaller datasets, returns default resolution. subsample focal points used benchmarking keep tuning fast still representative actual query performance.
